title: Spliting of mobile mandibular incisors in periodontitis patients using customized zirconia splints and their impact on Oral Health–Related Quality of Life
summary: A common symptom of severe periodontitis is the progressive mobility of affected teeth, which may lead to an impairment of quality of life. In this study, patients with periodontitis who present with pronounced mobility of the mandibular incisors will receive stabilization of these teeth using an individualized, 3D-printed, fixed splint made of zirconia. The aim of the study is to determine the survival rate of these splints after 1 and 2 years and to evaluate their impact on oral health–related quality of life.

interventions.name: This clinical prospective single-arm pilot study will include 20 adult patients with periodontitis and pathologically mobile mandibular incisors who are able to provide informed consent.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Age ≥ 18 years, ≥ 12 remaining teeth, periodontitis Stage III/IV, no active periodontal therapy within the past 2 years, informed consent, at least one mandibular incisor with mobility Grade II or III in combination with a clinical attachment loss (CAL) ≥ 5 mm and at least 50% relative alveolar bone loss at the affected tooth.
Exclusion criteria:
Pregnancy, pronounced bruxism,  region of teeth 33 to 43: a crossbite, overbite, the presence of implants
